subject: Mathematics: Analysis & Approaches

stem:
A grouped distribution has class frequencies 4,9,18,15,10,4 for equal-width classes
[140,145),...,[165,170). Estimate the median, Q1 and Q3 using interpolation. [7]
questions.title: Cumulative frequency

stem: A function has f'(x)=x^3-4x. Find where f is decreasing. [4]
questions.title: Intervals of decrease
solution: f'=x(x-2)(x+2). A sign chart gives f'<0 on (-infinity,-2) union (0,2).

stem: A wheel has radius 24 m, centre 27 m high and period 8 min. A rider starts at the lowest point. Form a cosine model and find the first time the rider is 39 m high. [6]
questions.title: Ferris-wheel modelling
solution: h=27-24cos(pi t/4). Set h=39: cos(pi t/4)=-1/2. The first positive solution is pi t/4=2pi/3, so t=8/3 min.

stem: Let g(x)=x^3-3x+2sin x. Find its local maximum A and minimum B, then find the area enclosed by the curve and chord AB. [7]
questions.title: Numerical calculus and area
solution: Solving g'=3x^2-3+2cosx=0 gives A=(-0.700,0.469) and B=(0.700,-0.469). The chord is y=-0.669x. It meets the curve at x=-0.700,0,0.700. Numerical integration of the absolute difference gives total enclosed area 0.0814.

stem: X is normal. P(X>72)=0.30 and P(X>80 | X>72)=0.20. Find mu and sigma. [7]
questions.title: Normal distribution parameters

stem: Water enters a conical tank of height 9 m and radius 3 m at 2 m^3/min. Find dh/dt when the water depth is 6 m. [4]
questions.title: Related rates
solution: Similarity gives r/h=1/3. V=(1/3)pi(h/3)^2h=pi h^3/27. Thus dV/dt=(pi h^2/9)dh/dt. At h=6, 2=4pi dh/dt, so dh/dt=1/(2pi) m/min.

stem: A density is f(x)=kx for 0<=x<=a and f(x)=k(6-x) for a<x<=6, continuous at a.
questions.title: Continuous probability density
solution: Continuity gives ka=k(6-a), so a=3. Total area is two triangles: 2(1/2)(3)(3k)=9k=1, so k=1/9. By symmetry about x=3, E(X)=3.

parts.label: b
parts.html: Plot them and find the area of their triangle in the Argand plane.

questions.title: Complex numbers
solution: The conjugate 2-3i is a root. Their quadratic is z^2-4z+13, and division gives the remaining factor z-1. The roots are 1, 2+3i, 2-3i. In the Argand plane the vertical base has length 6 and the perpendicular distance from (1,0) to Re(z)=2 is 1, so the area is 3.

stem: The upper semicircle x^2+(y-2)^2=16 is y=2+sqrt(16-x^2).

parts.label: b
parts.html: Use the arc-length formula to find the length from x=0 to x=4.

questions.title: Arc length and integration
solution: dy/dx=-x/sqrt(16-x^2). Then sqrt(1+(y')^2)=4/sqrt(16-x^2). The length is integral_0^4 4/sqrt(16-x^2) dx=4[arcsin(x/4)]_0^4=2pi.

stem: An account starts with $25 000 and earns 4.6% nominal interest compounded monthly. An asset costs $42 000 and depreciates by 5% annually.

parts.label: c
parts.html: Determine the first year the account exceeds the asset value.

questions.title: Financial modelling
solution: A_n=25000(1+0.046/12)^(12n), C_n=42000(0.95)^n. Substitution gives A_6=$32 929 and C_6=$30 874. Checking consecutive integer years shows n=5 is insufficient and n=6 is sufficient, so the first year is 2032.

stem: Points A(1,-2,0), B(5,1,2), C(-1,3,4) define a triangular base. Vertex V(2,1,9).

parts.label: b
parts.html: Find the perpendicular height from V to the plane.

parts.label: c
parts.html: Find the base area and tetrahedral volume.

parts.label: d
parts.html: Find the angle between VA and the plane.

questions.title: Three-dimensional vectors and a cone
solution:
AB=(4,3,2), AC=(-2,5,4). AB cross AC=(2,-20,26)=2(1,-10,13). Plane: (1,-10,13) dot ((x,y,z)-(1,-2,0))=0, so x-10y+13z-21=0. Height=|2-10+117-21|/sqrt270=88/sqrt270. Base area=1/2|AB cross
AC|=sqrt270. Volume=(1/3)(sqrt270)(88/sqrt270)=88/3. For the angle alpha between VA and the plane, sin alpha=|VA dot n|/(|VA||n|), with VA=(-1,-3,-9), n=(1,-10,13).

parts.label: a
parts.html: Find the condition on a,b for lim(x->-1) f(x) to be finite, and evaluate the limit.

parts.label: b
parts.html: Otherwise find the vertical and oblique asymptotes.

parts.label: c
parts.html: For a=-3,b=2, sketch f and f(|x|).

questions.title: Rational functions and absolute inequalities
solution:
Finite limit requires numerator(-1)=1-a+b=0, so b=a-1; cancellation then gives the finite limit a-2. In general division gives f=x+(a-1)+(b-a+1)/(x+1), so asymptotes are x=-1 and y=x+a-1 unless cancellation occurs. For a=-3,b=2, f=(x^2-3x+2)/(x+1)=x-4+6/(x+1). For x>=0, f(|x|)=f(x), so strict inequality is impossible. For x<0, f(-x)-f(x)=2x(x^2+5)/(1-x^2). A sign chart gives the solution
-1<x<0.
